items.title: Children in camp for IS-linked families speak about attempt to get to Australia
items.description: The children of women with ISIS links stuck in a Syrian refugee camp talk about their attempt to leave last week, saying they dream of one day buying toys and ice cream in Australia.

items.title: Children of 'ISIS brides' become a political hot potato
items.description: The fate of the "ISIS brides" is inextricably linked to constitutional facts but the debate about their future is not taking place in a legal chamber — it is being fought in the court of public opinion.

items.title: Hundreds join support group in wake of claims against gynaecologist
items.description: More former patients of Melbourne gynaecologist Simon Gordon have come forward to express distress over their treatment with many joining a newly-formed private support group.

items.title: 'A patronising cop out': Grace Tame responds to PM 'difficult life' apology
items.description: Grace Tame has criticised Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's qualified apology after he described her as "difficult", saying "what a patronising cop out".

items.title: Three people injured after suspected lightning strikes during Perth storm
items.description: Two teenage girls and a man in his 70s are receiving medical care after lightning strikes in Perth.

items.title: 'It was sadistic': Victim's anger as teen who attacked him walked free
items.description: A suspected serial violent homophobe linked to an Islamic State terrorist network walks free on probation after pleading guilty to a brutal snuff-video-style gay bashing.

items.title: Australians will receive mobile alert in July under new emergency trial
items.description: Most Australians will receive a mobile phone alert in July this year, as part of a nationwide test of a new emergency warning system.

items.title: Hearing reveals 'culture of carelessness' at Optus ahead of Triple Zero deaths
items.description: A Senate committee hears bombshell testimony about Optus's processes during an outage that led to the deaths of multiple customers who were unable to call Triple Zero.

items.title: Teen confirmed as first Australian death from tick-induced red meat allergy
items.description: Jeremy Webb's death in 2022 is the first documented fatal case of mammalian meat allergy in the country and second in the world.

items.title: Live: Middle East situation 'fast-moving', deputy PM says
items.description: Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles says the situation in the Middle East is "fast-moving" as the government moves to evacuate dependents of Australian diplomats from Israel and Lebanon. Follow live.

items.title: Subcontractor jailed for fatal gas mix-up at Sydney hospital
items.description: Newborn John Ghanem died, while baby Amelia Khan suffered severe and permanent brain damage when they were inadvertently given nitrous oxide instead of oxygen after their births.

items.title: Mother and daughter discover contender for world's largest known coral colony
items.description: Mother and daughter citizen scientists have found what is believed to be the largest coral colony on the Great Barrier Reef and possibly in the world.

items.title: Accused in Sydney grandfather's killing 'no mastermind', lawyer says
items.description: Two men are charged over the alleged kidnapping and death of Sydney grandfather Chris Baghsarian.

items.title: Trump says Muslim congresswomen should be removed from US over speech clash
items.description: US President Donald Trump says two Muslim Democratic politicians should be sent back to "where they came" from after a heated exchange during his State of the Union address.

items.title: Preaching kindness, Amanda Seyfried went all in on her latest role
items.description: The Oscar-nominated star adored working with director Mona Fastvold to resurrect an astonishing religious figure in The Testament of Ann Lee.

items.title: INXS nominated for induction into Rock & Roll Hall of Fame
items.description: INXS will be considered for induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame and is one of 10 first-time nominees on the ballot.

items.title: From the first Mardi Gras to RuPaul, do you know your queer history?
items.description: Australia's LGBTQIA+ history is full to the brim with groundbreaking art, brave protests and lots of fun along the way. Test how much you know about the queer trailblazers of our country in this quiz.

items.title: Basil Zempilas apologises to female MP who felt 'intimidated' by him
items.description: WA Opposition Leader Basil Zempilas apologises to a Labor backbencher who says she felt "intimidated" by him when he stood over her in parliament on Wednesday afternoon.

items.title: Qantas shares fall more than 6 per cent after first-half profit announced
items.description: Qantas' first-half profit result has disappointed shareholders, but chief executive Vanessa Hudson says the airline's largest fleet renewal in history will pay off.

items.title: National bushfire outlook puts NSW, Victoria and southern WA at heightened risk
items.description: The latest seasonal bushfire outlook has identified large parts of Victoria, NSW and southern WA as still at risk, even though summer is almost over.

items.title: Chess at the SCG? Lofty ambitions touted as world champion visits
items.description: Five-time World Chess Champion Viswanathan Anand says he believes Australia could be on the verge of becoming a proud chess nation.

items.title: Pro-democracy Hong Kong media mogul Jimmy Lai's fraud offence overturned
items.description: Hong Kong's Court of Appeal overturns the lower court ruling against Jimmy Lai on a fraud offence.

items.title: US tariffs on Australia remain at 10 per cent — for now
items.description: Trade Minister Don Farrell hopes Australia can dodge a higher tariff rate being imposed by the US, saying trade officials overnight confirmed the tariff rate on Australia would remain at 10 per cent — at least for now.

items.title: RBA governor says she does not think inflation is taking off again
items.description: Michelle Bullock gives more details on how quickly developments affecting monetary policy have moved since the middle of last year.

items.title: How shed boxes became one of the most precious collections in Australia
items.description: The ABC gets a rare look at the Aboriginal History Archive, a little-known collection of thousands of items collected by the well-known activist Gary Foley.
